title: research: diffusion policy for insertion tasks
description:
## Source
- Diffusion Policy (Chi et al. 2023): https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.04137
- DIPCOM for bimanual insertion: recent work on compliance + diffusion
- One-Step Diffusion Policy (2025): competitive inference speed

## What It Is
Diffusion models iteratively refine actions from random noise (like image 
diffusion but for robot actions). They can represent multi-modal action 
distributions — when there are multiple valid ways to approach the port, 
diffusion captures ALL of them instead of averaging (which is what ACT does).

## Relevance to Our Task
Our ~5cm alignment error may be because ACT averages across different board
configs. Diffusion policy handles multi-modality naturally. Papers show 46.9%
improvement over baselines on contact-rich tasks.

## Implementation Plan
- LeRobot has DiffusionPolicy implementation
- Keep our ResNet-18 encoder, swap transformer decoder for diffusion head
- Retrain on same 24 demos

## Validation Before Trying
- Check if LeRobot's DiffusionPolicy works with our data format
- Compare inference speed (needs <250ms per step for real-time)
- Run micro-train (20 epochs) first to see signal

## Effort: Medium | Risk: Medium | Potential: High

title: exp-057: V2 collector with P-controller velocity actions
description:
## Results: 3/300 — REGRESSION
P-controller velocity (K_lin=2.0) generates actions 10x larger than observed
TCP velocity. Causes 163N force spikes and 16cm overshoot.

## Analysis
- V2 action std: z=0.073 vs V1 z=0.008 (9.6x larger)
- The velocity-mode controller can't safely track 0.26 m/s commands
- Need K_lin ≈ 0.2 to match V1 scale, but that defeats the purpose

## Conclusion: DISCARD
The P-controller approach needs careful gain tuning. The observed TCP
velocity (V1 data) is actually the right signal — it represents what
the impedance controller can safely execute. The issue isn't signal
strength but signal structure (temporal dynamics, not magnitude).

## Revised understanding
The v5 model (152.9) already achieves partial insertion. The path to
full insertion is likely more training data diversity + correct epoch
count, not different action representation.

title: exp-003-a1: fix forward direction + try all 6 axes
description:

SC trial completely different geometry. 26x improvement over exp-001.

description:

The lower friction changes insertion dynamics. New training data

title: research: one-step diffusion policy (fast inference)
description:
## Source
- One-Step Diffusion Policy (2025)
- Distills multi-step diffusion into single forward pass

## What It Is
Regular diffusion needs 10-100 denoising steps per action (slow). One-step
distillation gets the quality of diffusion in a single forward pass, matching
ACT inference speed.

## Relevance
If we try diffusion policy and it's too slow, this is the solution.
Only relevant if bd-10f (diffusion policy) shows promise first.

## Effort: Hard | Risk: Medium | Potential: High (if diffusion works)

title: exp-004-a3: compliant insertion with force feedback
description:
## Hypothesis
Once aligned with the port (from A1 or A2), the insertion phase requires
compliance. Low stiffness + force monitoring should allow the connector
to slide into the port without excessive force. A spiral search pattern
can compensate for small alignment errors.

## Branch
A3 (classical control, force-feedback insertion)

## Changes Planned
- After approach phase, switch to low stiffness
- Monitor wrench for contact detection
- Implement spiral search if initial push fails
- Gradual Z descent with XY compliance

## Expected Outcome
- Tier 3: 50-75 (partial to full insertion)
- No force penalties

title: exp-003-a2: camera-based port detection
description:
## Hypothesis
The 3 wrist cameras (left, center, right) at 1152x1024 provide enough
visual information to detect the target port. If we can estimate port
pose from images, we can servo toward it without ground truth.

## Branch
A2 (classical control, vision-based)

## Changes Planned
- Capture camera images from observations
- Try template matching / feature detection for port location
- Estimate port pose relative to camera frame
- Command robot to align with detected port

## Expected Outcome
- Port detection working -> proximity points
- Depends on A1 results showing approach strategy works

title: exp-059: v11 weighted insertion sampling (3x)
description:
## Results: 115.4/300 — WORSE than v5 (152.9)
3x insertion weight degraded approach quality while slightly
improving insertion phase. Classic quality tradeoff.

## Conclusion: DISCARD
3x is too aggressive. v5 (unweighted, 100 epochs) remains best.
Could try 1.5x weight as a gentler balance.

exp-043: data augmentation (image jitter + noise during training)
description:
## Results
| Trial | Augmented | Baseline | Delta |
|-------|-----------|----------|-------|
| 1 (SFP) | 30.2 | 44.0 | -13.8 |
| 2 (SFP) | 30.5 | 44.0 | -13.5 |
| 3 (SC) | 27.7 | 26.4 | +1.3 |
| **Total** | **88.4** | **114.4** | **-26.0** |

## Analysis
DISCARD. Augmentation (brightness, contrast, noise) significantly hurt.
Best checkpoint val_loss 0.153 vs 0.136 non-augmented.

The visual patterns for port localization are precise — the model needs
exact pixel-level features. Random brightness/contrast destroys these.

The augmentation prevents overfitting (training can continue past 50 epochs
without divergence) but the resulting model generalizes WORSE, not better.
This suggests overfitting to the training images is actually helpful here —
the model needs to memorize the port appearance.

## Lesson
For this task, data augmentation hurts because the visual precision required
for port localization is disrupted by image perturbations. The bottleneck
isn't overfitting to images — it's the diversity of board positions.

title: human: set up OVH L4-90 cloud instance
description:
## Steps to Set Up OVH L4-90 Cloud GPU Instance

### 1. Create the Instance on OVH

1. Go to https://us.ovhcloud.com/public-cloud/prices/
2. Create a Public Cloud project (if you don't have one)
3. Launch an instance:
   - **Flavor**: L4-90 ($1.00/hr)
   - **Region**: Pick closest to you (US-EAST for lowest latency to AWS ECR)
   - **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04
   - **SSH Key**: Add your public key during creation
     - If you need to generate one: `cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub`
     - Copy that into the OVH SSH key field
   - **Name**: something like `aic-gpu`
4. Note the public IP address once it's running

### 2. On THIS machine: Add SSH config

```bash
cat >> ~/.ssh/config << 'EOF2'

Host gpu
    HostName <ovh-instance-ip>
    User ubuntu
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
    ForwardAgent yes
EOF2
```

Replace `<ovh-instance-ip>` with the actual IP.

Test: `ssh gpu echo "connected"`

### 3. On THIS machine: Run the setup script on the GPU instance

```bash
scp scripts/gpu-setup.sh gpu:~/gpu-setup.sh
ssh gpu "chmod +x ~/gpu-setup.sh && ~/gpu-setup.sh"
```

This takes ~10-15 min. It installs:
- Pixi + ROS 2 Kilted + Gazebo
- Docker + NVIDIA Container Toolkit
- Creates ~/run-eval.sh
- Clones the repo (or prompts you to)
- Verifies GPU, Gazebo, ROS 2, Docker all work

### 4. Update runner config

Edit `scripts/runner-config.sh` on this machine:
```bash
GPU_HOST="gpu"
USE_REMOTE_EVAL="true"
```

### 5. Test end-to-end

```bash
scripts/remote-eval.sh aic_example_policies.ros.WaveArm
```

Should take ~5 min (vs 27 min locally). Expect WaveArm to score ~1/trial.

### 6. Run our first real experiment

```bash
scripts/remote-eval.sh aic_example_policies.ros.BlindPush
```

### 7. When done for the day

Stop the instance from OVH console to stop billing.
Storage persists -- next time just start it and SSH in.

## Cost Notes
- $1.00/hr while running
- Stop when not using it
- Storage persists when stopped (pennies/day)
- Budget ~$250 for entire qualification phase

title: exp-033: HybridPolicy (IBVS alignment + ACT insertion)
description:
## Hypothesis
IBVS alignment + ACT insertion would combine best of both approaches.

## Score: 120.6/300 (identical to pure ACT)
## Analysis
IBVS correction is ~1mm, ACT immediately overrides with its own trajectory.
The combination adds no value -- ACT dominates the behavior completely.
DISCARD. The bottleneck is ACT's action representation, not initial alignment.

title: exp-041: task encoding in observation (port_type + module_name)
description:
## Hypothesis
Model doesn't know which port to target. Adding port_type (sfp=0, sc=1) and
target_module encoding to the state vector tells the model what it's aiming for.

## Implementation
- DataCollector: append [port_type_int, module_idx] to state (28D instead of 26D)
- train_act.py: --state-dim 28
- OurACT: include task encoding in observation

## Expected Outcome
Especially helps SC trials where the port is in a different location.

title: exp-017-b: IBVS -- center port in camera, then descend
description:
## Hypothesis
IBVS -- center port in camera image using pixel error, then descend.

## Branch: B (IBVS)
## Score: 110.4/300 -- ALL-TIME HIGH (at the time)
## Results
| Trial | Distance | Notes |
|-------|---------|-------|
| 1 (SFP) | 6cm | Proximity + T2 |

title: infra: GPU audit + scope all work under ~/aic/
description:
## Goal
When the GPU comes back up, perform a full audit + cleanup + namespace
isolation so our work doesn't conflict with other agents sharing the box.
The local machine has already been consolidated into ~/aic/ on 2026-04-25;
this bead aligns the GPU to the same convention.

## Target layout (matches LOCAL after 2026-04-25 cleanup)

```
~/aic/
├── src/                  # GPU only: rsync target for the repo
├── data/
│   ├── velocity/         # was ~/training_data_velocity (~9.2GB, 126 eps)
│   └── lowfriction/      # was ~/training_data_lowfriction (~7.7GB, 45 eps)
├── models/               # was ~/aic_models (v5, v12, lowfriction_v1, combined_v1)
├── results/              # was ~/aic_results (scoring.yaml output)
├── logs/                 # train/eval stdout
└── bin/run-eval.sh       # was ~/run-eval.sh
```

Shared in home (keep):
- ~/.pixi/
- distrobox containers (global)

## Audit checklist (run when GPU comes up)
1. `df -h` — disk available
2. `ls -la ~` — surprise files from other agents
3. `distrobox list` — containers present + health
4. `ls ~/.pixi/bin/` — pixi version
5. `nvidia-smi` — GPU health, VRAM free
6. `ps aux | grep -E 'pixi|python|ros'` — orphan processes to kill
7. Look for orphan tmp files in /tmp, /var/tmp

## Cleanup + migration on GPU
1. `mkdir -p ~/aic/{src,data,models,results,logs,bin}`
2. `mv ~/training_data_velocity ~/aic/data/velocity`
3. `mv ~/training_data_lowfriction ~/aic/data/lowfriction`
4. `mv ~/aic_models ~/aic/models`  (or `mv ~/aic_models/* ~/aic/models/`
   if ~/aic/models already has content)
5. `mv ~/aic_results ~/aic/results` if present
6. `mv ~/run-eval.sh ~/aic/bin/run-eval.sh` and update its internal paths
   (RESULTS_DIR, MODEL_DIR if hardcoded)
7. First rsync from local: target is `gpu:~/aic/src/`, exclude data/models/results/logs

## Verification
- Cold eval of v5 baseline from new paths → score should land in 110-170 range
  (per the variance check in experiment-log.md)
- Confirm no writes outside ~/aic/ during a train+eval cycle (`find ~ -newer ~/aic/.audit-stamp -not -path '~/aic/*'`)

## Why this matters
GPU is ~$1/hr and shared. Isolation prevents collisions and matches the local
~/aic/ convention so absolute paths work identically on both machines.
notes: 2026-04-26 status: LOCAL side fully complete (commit 9c60885 consolidated all aic-related dirs under ~/aic/). GPU side blocked — SSH to gpu times out (instance suspended/down). When GPU returns, run the audit + migration checklist above. Orphan check flagged this bead because the opening commit (3cda8f8) referenced it; that's expected for a multi-stage infra bead with the GPU half still pending.

title: spec: OVH cloud runner architecture
cleanup: prune Docker images and reclaim disk space
description:
## Context
Docker images and build cache consume significant disk space on this machine.
After migrating eval to the Mac Studio, we can reclaim this space.

## Task
1. Stop any running containers: `docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yaml down`
2. Report current disk usage:
   - `docker system df -v`
   - `df -h /`
3. Prune everything:
   - `docker system prune -a --volumes` (removes all images, containers, volumes, build cache)
4. Report reclaimed space:
   - `docker system df -v` (should show ~0)
   - `df -h /` (compare before/after)
5. Provide summary report:
   - Space before cleanup
   - Space after cleanup
   - Space reclaimed
   - Remaining Docker footprint (if any)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All unused Docker images removed
- [ ] Build cache cleared
- [ ] Report showing before/after disk usage
- [ ] At least 40GB reclaimed (eval 9.5GB + model 13.7GB + cache 34GB)

## Notes
- Do NOT run this until the Mac runner is confirmed working
- The eval image would need to be re-pulled (~10 min) if we ever need local Docker again
- The model image rebuild would take ~5 min

title: exp-056: v6 200 epochs - push for full insertion
description:
## Results: 83.9/300 — REGRESSION (OVERFITTING)
v6 (200 epochs) WORSE than v5 (100 epochs, 152.9).
Trial 1 regressed from partial insertion to 14cm away.

## Overfitting confirmed
- Loss dropped to 0.031 (vs v5's 0.037) but score dropped by 69 points
- Model memorized training configs, lost generalization
- Lower loss ≠ better eval score — exactly as predicted

## Conclusion: DISCARD v6, keep v5 (100 epochs) as best
100 epochs is the sweet spot for 66 episodes at lr=5e-6.
More epochs → overfitting. Need MORE DATA not more epochs.

title: exp-038: offset actions + weight decay to prevent overfitting
description:
## Hypothesis
Weight decay prevents overfitting for 39-demo/50-epoch training.

## Score: 120.9/300 (but likely randomization variance)
## Analysis
SAME score as several other evals (120.9). Confirmed this is NOT stale code --
--no-cache rebuild produces same score. The 120.9 vs 136.0 difference is
randomization variance (~15 points), not model quality.

The position-mode models (exp-034: 131, exp-035: 136) are our best but
scores vary 120-136 per run. True average is probably ~128.

All recent evals at 5cm/5cm/10cm distances = consistent model behavior.
KEEP (matches best models within variance).

title: impl: update all skills/docs for cloud runner
exp-050: first fine-tuned velocity ACT eval
description:
## Results: 86.1/300 (from -21 pretrained baseline)
| Trial | Tier1 | Tier2 | Tier3 | Total | Distance |
|-------|-------|-------|-------|-------|----------|
| 1 SFP | 1 | 18.0 | 25.0 | 44.0 | 0.05m |
| 2 SFP | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1.0 | 0.14m |
| 3 SC  | 1 | 18.0 | 22.1 | 41.1 | 0.03m |

## Analysis
- Massive improvement over pretrained (-21 → 86.1)
- Model learned approach trajectory (smooth, efficient)
- Gets very close (3-5cm) but doesn't insert
- Trial 2 regression: different config not learned
- No contacts, no force penalties → safe behavior
- Training: 50 epochs, 21 episodes (2229 steps), final loss 0.062

## Key Issue
The model stops ~3-5cm from the port. The fine insertion phase
needs more precise velocity commands. Possible causes:
1. Recording at 4Hz loses the fine-grained insertion dynamics
2. The observed TCP velocity during CheatCode's position-mode
   control may not capture the last-mile insertion velocity
3. Need more diverse training data (trial 2 missed)

## Next Steps
1. Collect more data (especially diverse configs)
2. Try higher recording frequency (10Hz instead of 4Hz)
3. Try computing velocity from position differences instead of TCP velocity
4. Increase time limit (currently 30s like RunACT)

title: exp-032: ACT v8 diverse42 (42 demos, 14 configs) -- TRAINING
description:
## Hypothesis
42 episodes from 14 configs (vs 27 from 8) will break past 121.9 plateau.

## Training
- Data: 42 episodes, 14 configs
- val_loss: 16.9 (vs 13.7 for v6 -- higher due to more diverse validation set)
- 100 epochs, 73s/epoch, ~2 hours

## Score: 120.6/300
| Trial | Duration | Distance | Notes |
|-------|----------|---------|-------|
| 1 (SFP) | 1.1s | 5cm | Same as v6 |
| 2 (SFP) | 1.1s | 5cm | Same as v6 |
| 3 (SC) | 1.3s | 10cm | Slightly worse than v6 (7cm) |

## Analysis
PLATEAU CONFIRMED at ~120. More configs (8→14) gave no improvement.
The bottleneck is NOT data diversity beyond 8 configs.
Possible bottlenecks: model architecture, action representation (velocity vs position),
or the 5cm final gap is a fundamental limit of our approach.

Next: try position-mode actions, larger model, or HybridPolicy.

title: exp-019-b: two-pass IBVS -- align, descend, realign, insert
exp-045: lower stiffness for compliant insertion
description:
## Results
| Trial | Stiffness | Baseline | Delta |
|-------|-----------|----------|-------|
| 1 (SFP) | 44.0 | 44.0 | 0.0 |
| 2 (SFP) | 37.1 | 44.0 | -6.9 |
| 3 (SC) | 30.4 | 26.4 | +4.0 |
| **Total** | **111.5** | **114.4** | **-2.9** |

## Analysis
DISCARD. Lower Z stiffness after step 120 caused drift during approach.
Step 120 = 30s, but the approach phase takes 40-50s. The compliance kicked
in while the robot was still positioning, causing accuracy loss.

SC trial improved slightly (+4 pts) — compliance may help for insertion
but the approach needs to be precise first.

Revert stiffness to default. Consider Z-only compliance ONLY after detecting
proximity (via position, not timestep). But this requires more sophistication.

title: research: CCIL corrective imitation learning
description:
## Source
- CCIL: Continuity-based Corrective Imitation Learning
- Generates corrective actions using local dynamics continuity

## What It Is
Learns a dynamics model from demos, then generates corrective actions for
states near (but not on) the expert trajectory. These corrections point
BACK toward the expert path. Training on original + corrective data makes
the policy more robust to perturbations.

## Relevance to Our Task
Our policy drifts from the expert trajectory, ending up ~5cm from the port.
CCIL directly addresses trajectory drift by teaching the model to self-correct.

## Implementation Plan
1. Fit linear dynamics model from our 24 trajectories
2. Perturb states slightly off-trajectory (add noise to state)
3. Generate corrective actions that would return to trajectory
4. Augment dataset with these synthetic corrections
5. Retrain

## Validation
- First verify that adding state noise + corrections improves val_loss
- Check if corrective data reduces trajectory drift during eval

## Effort: Medium | Risk: Low-Medium | Potential: Medium

title: exp-058: longer episodes + smaller chunk alignment
description:
## Hypothesis
The v5 baseline (66 eps, 100 epochs, lr=5e-6, batch=8) was data-limited:
the v6 regression at 200 epochs (83.9/300) showed overfitting on 66 eps.
Doubling the dataset to 126 eps should let the model see more pose/board
configurations and generalize better, EITHER at 100 epochs (same compute,
more data → better generalization) OR at 150 epochs (more data tolerates
longer training).

The "smaller chunk alignment" half of the original title is descoped
from this bead — see Future Work below. We'll change ONE variable here
per /experiment discipline.

## Baseline (the only thing this experiment measures against)
- v5: 66 eps, 100 epochs, lr=5e-6, batch=8, weight_decay=1e-4, grad_clip=10.0,
  insertion_weight=1.0, velocity-mode high-friction data, 30s trial limit
- Score: 110-170/300 pixi (median ~140), 124.2/300 Docker-verified

## Variable changed (exactly one)
- Dataset size: 66 → 126 episodes
- All other hyperparameters held at v5 values
- Output dir: ~/aic/models/act_velocity_v8

## Expected Outcome
- More data + same epochs (100): v8 lands 130-180/300 (overlaps top of v5
  range; main gain is reduced variance across runs)
- /experiment KEEP threshold: ≥5-point mean improvement over v5 across
  3 seeds = ≥145/300 mean

## Open question for orchestrator (resolve before dispatch)
~/aic/data/velocity now contains 126 eps total. v5 used 66. Is the
delta (60 eps) the same data distribution or was some collected
differently? If different distribution, we may be running an exp-062
repeat (combined-data regression to 50/300). VERIFY before training:
- Compare collection metadata between first 66 and last 60 episodes
- Confirm all 126 are pixi-collected, ground_truth=true, high-friction
- If mixed: split into clean 66+60 and train on the consistent set only

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Pre-flight: /audit-train passes on scripts/train_act.py
- [ ] Pre-flight: 126-episode data integrity verified (single distribution)
- [ ] Train command launched via nohup on GPU (per /train SKILL):
      pixi run python scripts/train_act.py
        --data-dir ~/aic/data/velocity
        --output-dir ~/aic/models/act_velocity_v8
        --epochs 100 --batch-size 8 --lr 5e-6
        --val-frac 0.2 --patience 10 --seed 42
- [ ] Training history.json shows val_loss curve (no silent divergence)
- [ ] 3-seed eval per /eval — mean + range vs v5
- [ ] Bead updated with full results table + analysis
- [ ] refs/experiment-log.md appended with exp-058 section
- [ ] KEEP/DISCARD verdict committed; if KEEP, /train SKILL baseline updated

## Future Work (out of scope for this bead)
- exp-NNN "smaller chunk alignment": investigate ACT chunk_size/n_action_steps
  sampling. Currently chunk_size=100; trying chunk_size=50 or different
  stride could change what the policy attends to. Open a separate bead
  if exp-058 succeeds AND we want to push further on the architecture side.

| 3 (SC) | 26.0 | 26.4 | -0.4 |
| **Total** | **106.1** | **114.4** | **-8.3** |

Training: best val_loss 0.168 (epoch 32) vs baseline 0.136.

## Analysis
DISCARD. Oversampling end-of-episode (last 150 timesteps 3x) degraded overall
trajectory quality. The model needs to learn the full approach equally — the
approach trajectory quality matters as much as the final alignment.

## Lesson
The model already focuses naturally on the insertion phase because those
timesteps have the hardest predictions (highest loss). Artificial oversampling
just imbalances the training.

| 3 (SC) | 1.0 | 26.4 | -25.4 |
| **Total** | **10.8** | **114.4** | **-103.6** |

Training: val_loss 0.081 (40% better than baseline 0.136).
107 episodes from 33+ configs. 50 epochs.

## Analysis
MASSIVE REGRESSION despite dramatically better val_loss. The new Docker-
collected data has different characteristics from the original pixi-collected
data. Possible causes:
1. Docker collect_config mount changes the sim behavior
2. The new random configs produce trajectories in a different coordinate frame
3. Mixing old and new data creates inconsistent training signal
4. The original data had ground_truth TF behavior that Docker doesn't replicate

## Lesson
val_loss improvement does NOT guarantee score improvement. The training
distribution must match the evaluation distribution. Collecting data through
a different pipeline (Docker vs pixi) creates distribution shift.

## Next
Revert to baseline model. Investigate WHY Docker-collected data differs.
Try training on ONLY the new data (without old) to isolate the issue.

title: human: set up Mac Studio as remote eval runner
description:
## Steps to Set Up Your Mac Studio M1 Max as the Primary Dev + Submission Machine

### 1. On THIS machine (dev host): Generate SSH key

```bash
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "aic-runner" -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
# Press enter for no passphrase (or set one)
```

### 2. On the Mac Studio: Enable Remote Login

1. System Settings → General → Sharing
2. Enable Remote Login (SSH)
3. Note the IP address (e.g., 192.168.1.50) or hostname (mac-studio.local)

### 3. On THIS machine: Copy SSH key to Mac

```bash
ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 <username>@<mac_ip>
# Test: ssh <username>@<mac_ip> echo "SSH works"
```

### 4. On THIS machine: Add SSH config

```bash
cat >> ~/.ssh/config << 'EOF2'

Host mac
    HostName <mac_ip_or_hostname>
    User <username>
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
    ForwardAgent yes
EOF2
```

Test: `ssh mac echo "config works"`

### 5. On the Mac: Install Xcode CLI Tools

```bash
xcode-select --install
```

### 6. On the Mac: Install Homebrew

```bash
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"
```

### 7. On the Mac: Install Docker Desktop

Download from https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/
(needed for final submission builds only, not for iteration)

### 8. From THIS machine: Run setup script on Mac

```bash
scp scripts/mac-setup.sh mac:~/mac-setup.sh
ssh mac "chmod +x ~/mac-setup.sh && ~/mac-setup.sh"
```

Takes ~10-20 min. Installs Pixi, ROS 2, Gazebo, creates ~/run-eval.sh.

### 9. Update runner config

Edit scripts/runner-config.sh: set MAC_HOST="mac"

### 10. Test end-to-end

```bash
scripts/remote-eval.sh aic_example_policies.ros.WaveArm
```

Should rsync code, run eval on Mac, fetch scoring.yaml back.

## Architecture

Mac Studio = everything:
- Native pixi + Gazebo for fast iteration (~10 min eval)
- Docker Desktop for submission builds (one-shot, not iteration)
- This machine = code editing + orchestration via SSH

title: research: JUICER bottleneck-aware data augmentation
description:
## Source
- JUICER (2024): "Learning from Bottleneck States" - synthetic data at 
  high-precision decision points
- Key insight: not all timesteps are equal; insertion alignment is the bottleneck

## What It Is
Identifies which states in trajectories are "bottlenecks" (require highest
precision). Generates synthetic corrective data specifically around those states.
With just 10 demos achieved strong results on 4-5 part assembly.

## Relevance to Our Task
Our model approaches well but fails at alignment/insertion. The last ~50
timesteps of each trajectory are the bottleneck. We could:
1. Oversample last 20% of trajectories (3x weight in loss)
2. Generate synthetic perturbations near insertion point
3. Add noise to state + require model to recover

## Implementation Plan
- Modify train_act.py to weight loss by timestep (higher for later steps)
- Or: duplicate final 100 timesteps of each episode in the dataset
- No new data collection needed

## Validation
- Check if overweighting end-of-episode improves val_loss for last-50 subset
- Compare proximity scores before/after

## Effort: Easy | Risk: Low | Potential: Medium

direction vector from TCP to port. Moving along that vector should get us
proximity points (0-25) and possibly partial insertion.

simple approach-toward-port works, before we invest in camera perception.

title: exp-039: offset actions (relative position, not absolute)
description:
## Hypothesis
Offset actions (delta from current TCP) should generalize better than absolute
positions across randomized board configs. Data analysis showed offset variance
is 2-3x lower than absolute position variance.

## Implementation
- convert_to_offsets.py: offline conversion of existing 39 episodes
- SimpleACT extracted to simple_act.py (fixes Docker import)
- OurACT offset mode: adds predicted delta to current TCP position
- Fixed Docker: gpus:all, ACT_MODEL_DIR, correct volume mount, argument order bug

## Training
- 50 epochs on 39 offset episodes
- Best val_loss: 0.130 (epoch 38) vs 0.17 for position mode
- train_loss: 0.064

## Results
| Trial | Score | Notes |
|-------|-------|-------|
| 1 (SFP) | 38.9 | Proximity only |
| 2 (SFP) | 41.7 | Proximity only |
| 3 (SC) | 31.0 | Proximity only |
| **Total** | **111.6** | **REGRESSION from 136.0** |

## Analysis
Despite lower val_loss (0.130 vs 0.17), offset actions scored WORSE than
absolute positions. Possible reasons:
1. **Error accumulation**: Each offset prediction adds to the current position.
   Small errors compound over the ~500 timestep trajectory.
2. **Training on 39 episodes vs 24**: The position model used 24 episodes from
   8 configs (sweet spot). We trained on all 39. May need to match the 24-episode
   subset.
3. **Quaternion mismatch**: We kept quaternion absolute but position as offset.
   This inconsistency may confuse the model.

## Next
- DISCARD offset actions for now
- Try absolute position with data augmentation instead
- Or try XYZ-only prediction (drop quaternion from action space)
- First: verify position-mode baseline works in Docker (it never has!)
